intended_object: The Rayleigh–Ritz residual R = (I − P)(A + εt)|_𝒳 for the Davis–Kahan free-beam example (Section 9). Here 𝒳 is the two-dimensional affine trial subspace span{1, t} ⊂ L²(0,1] and P is the orthogonal projection onto it. The source is the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `(id − beamTrial.starProjection) ∘L beamResidual ε`. `beamResidual ε` is multiplication by `ε t` (through `beamSymbol`, which equals `ε·t` on (0,1]), composed with the inclusion of the trial subspace.

The docstring speaks of `(A + ε t) v`, while the code uses only `ε t · v`. For trial vectors the two agree. The free-free beam operator A = d⁴/dt⁴ with free boundary conditions has the affine functions 1 and t in its kernel. So for every v in the trial plane, (A + εt)v = εt·v. The module's route description relies on exactly this, and it is also why the residual is a bounded operator here. The map therefore equals the standard Rayleigh–Ritz residual (I − P)HQ for H = A + εt.

This is a construction about one specific concrete operator from the paper's numerical example, so specialising to it is not a generality problem. Mathlib has no general "Rayleigh–Ritz residual" definition to cite.
